title: Google to Face $3.2 Billion Damage Claims Over Ad-Tech Monopoly
summary: USA Today Co., Daily Mail General and Trust Plc and a class of large publishers can seek more than $3.2 billion in damages for harm caused by monopolization of advertising technology markets by Alphabet Inc.’s Google, a New York federal judge ruled.

title: Apple’s Upcoming Smart Home Device Won’t Record Video
summary: On this episode of the Power On podcast, Mark Gurman explains how Apple could pitch a video-free smart home camera with facial recognition as as an alternative to other smart home devices on the market. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Carney Invokes New Powers to Fast-Track Pacific Oil Pipeline
summary: Prime Minister Mark Carney is expediting regulatory approval for a new, high-capacity oil pipeline to expand Canada’s access to Asian markets, with the aim of starting construction in September 2027.

title: Apple Wants to Take Over Your Home. Is Siri AI Ready?
summary:
In the premiere episode of Power On, Mark Gurman and Bloomberg Tech Editor Vlad Savov discuss two of Apple’s most anticipated Fall releases. First, Mark shares his massive scoop on Apple’s long awaited push into the home and what makes their Siri AI-powered devices different from other smart home options. Then, Mark and Vlad consider if upgrading to the new iPhone 18 is worth it and question Apple’s reliance on influencer marketing.

Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord

Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Carlyle Warns Private Credit AI Push Runs Concentration Risk
summary: Private credit firms rushing to finance the artificial intelligence buildout risk encountering the same concentration problems that have plagued lenders exposed to software companies, according to Carlyle Group Inc.

title: SpaceX Launches Crew for NASA on Retiring Dragon Capsule
summary: SpaceX launched a new crew of four astronauts to the International Space Station on Thursday, as questions swirl over the company’s plans for the future of its human spaceflight program.

title: Carlyle Warns on AI Hype and Credit Risk Ahead
summary: Amid the AI boom, private credit is pouring into data centers and hyperscalers, but the risks are real.  Carlyle's Co-President Mark Jenkins joins Bloomberg Open Interest with a warning that  concentration in a single hot theme can mirror the "SaaS apocalypse," where everything looked diversified until volatility hit. He breaks down where AI credit risk is building, how complex data‑center contracts can fail, and why old‑school diversification still matters more than AI hype. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Are We Losing Control of AI? What’s Driving New Fears
summary: For years, as artificial intelligence has evolved from the stuff of sci-fi movies to an app ordinary people have installed on their phones, tech leaders and some AI insiders have talked about the potential for it to escape human control and wreak havoc on society. Those fears have become impossible to ignore in recent weeks, driven by advances in the technology, a series of cybersecurity breaches involving AI agents, and new warnings from rank-and-file AI staffers.

title: Netflix Isn't Growing Fast Enough, Sarandos Says
summary: Ted Sarandos said Netflix isn’t growing as quickly as he would like and the company is working on making that move faster. The co-chief executive officer speaks to Lucas Shaw at Bloomberg Screentime in Los Angeles. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: McCormick Climbs on Sales; Constellation Energy Gains on Amazon Deal | Stock Movers
summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- McCormick (MKC) shares rose after the company posted its strongest sales since 2021, with third-quarter net sales increasing 17% to $2.02 billion.
- Accenture (ACN) shares are moving higher after the IT services company reported fourth-quarter results that beat expectations on key metrics, including revenue and bookings.
- Constellation Energy (CEG) is gaining after the operator of gas power plants said it signed a 20-year power purchase agreement with Amazon, which covers 690 megawatts of nuclear capacity at Maryland’s Calvert Cliffs Clean Energy Center, including a 190-megawatt uprate. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Samsung Raises Prices of Most Galaxy S26 Smartphones by $100
summary: Samsung Electronics Co. raised prices across most of its Galaxy S26 smartphone lineup, the latest example of consumer-tech brands passing costs on to consumers amid a persistent memory shortage.

title: Tesla Sell Ratings Slide as Analysts Eye Musk’s AI Ambitions
summary: Tesla Inc. shares have tumbled in 2026, but Wall Street analysts are increasingly reluctant to tell investors to sell.

title: Odd Lots: Is the AI Trade Fed Rate Proof?
summary:
Is it safe to say that AI companies are less sensitive to Fed rate changes, making them a good investment during these times of market volatility?

Luke Kawa, head of markets at Sherwood News, joins Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal on the Odd Lots podcast to discuss all the big market themes and how the AI trade is affecting the sheer speed of market moves. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: ECB’s Lagarde Says Europe Must Develop Its Own AI Capabilities
summary: Europe risks leaving itself vulnerable if it relies on artificial intelligence models developed elsewhere, according to European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde.

title: Google Rolls Out AI Model Gemini 4 Argon
summary: Alphabet's Google has begun rolling out Gemini 4 Argon, its long-awaited flagship artificial intelligence model, but even some insiders say it has underperformed in some areas. Bloomberg's Carmen Reinicke reports. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Accenture’s Technology Clients Helped Revenue Beat Estimates
summary: Accenture Plc, the technology consulting firm that’s under pressure to show it can help clients adopt artificial intelligence and can undergo such a transition itself, reported that it booked more business in the fourth quarter than analysts had expected.

title: Microsoft’s Trillion-Dollar Quarter Powered by Ravenous AI Trade
summary: With Microsoft Corp.’s best quarter for decades in the books, Wall Street is betting the stock can keep rallying as the tech giant’s standing in the artificial intelligence landscape continues to improve.

title: TSMC Mulls Multibillion-Dollar Texas Site for More AI Chips
summary: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. is weighing a new campus in Texas that would add tens of billions of dollars in new investment to the company’s multiyear expansion into chipmaking in the US.

title: Amazon Debuts 2026 Kindles: 6-Inch Kindle, Paperwhite, Colorsoft
summary: Sales of the company’s e-readers are rising as the product line approaches its 20th anniversary next year.

title: Fed’s Kashkari on Rates, Inflation, Bond Yields, US Economy
summary: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis President Neel Kashkari says that the central bank “will do what we need to do to get inflation back down to our target.” He also addresses the strength of the US economy, lessons learned on supply shocks, and a potential signal from US two-year Treasury yields. (Source: Bloomberg)
